# Ghost display on reversed navigation (2026-02-04 19:16Z)

_**User**_

when the user navigates and has reversed the route/navigation there is a ghost still shown on the map driviing from the user device towards the other device.

In this case the ghost should not be shown. Showing the ghost is only valid when the navigation route is shown from the other device towards the user device (default when first enabling navigation)

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_


Investigating the ghost display logic. Searching for navigation reversal and ghost rendering code.

        "contents": "    static func ghost(for route: MKRoute, deviceTimestamp: Date?, knownDeviceSpeed: Double?, userTimestamp: Date?, knownUserSpeed: Double?, now: Date = Date(), isRouteReversed: Bool = false) -&gt; (MKPolyline, MKPolyline, CLLocationCoordinate2D, Double)? {\n        guard route.distance &gt; 0 else { return nil }\n        let totalDistance = route.distance\n        \n        // Only use speeds above the threshold to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices\n        let deviceSpeed = usableSpeed(knownDeviceSpeed)\n        let userSpeed = usableSpeed(knownUserSpeed)\n        \n        // Use the speed/timestamp of the journey start to keep progress aligned to route direction.\n        let primarySpeed = isRouteReversed ? deviceSpeed : userSpeed\n        let primaryTimestamp = isRouteReversed ? deviceTimestamp : userTimestamp\n        let secondaryTimestamp = isRouteReversed ? userTimestamp : deviceTimestamp\n        \n        let fallbackElapsed: TimeInterval\n        if let primaryTimestamp {\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(primaryTimestamp)\n        } else if let secondaryTimestamp {\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(secondaryTimestamp)\n        } else {\n            fallbackElapsed = 0\n        }\n        \n        let distanceFromStart: CLLocationDistance\n        if let speed = primarySpeed {\n            if let ts = primaryTimestamp {\n                let elapsed = max(0, now.timeIntervalSince(ts))\n                distanceFromStart = min(totalDistance, max(0, elapsed * speed))\n            } else {\n                // Without a timestamp we cannot project using speed; fall back to travel time\n                let expected = route.expectedTravelTime\n                let progress = expected &gt; 0 ? max(0, min(1, fallbackElapsed / expected)) : 0\n                distanceFromStart = totalDistance * progress\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Fallback: use expectedTravelTime proportion if available (start appears stationary)",

Falls back to MKRoute.expectedTravelTime otherwise.\n/// Speed values below the threshold are ignored to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices.\nstruct RouteGhostCalculator {\n    /// Minimum speed threshold in m/s to consider device as moving.\n    /// Values below this threshold are treated as GPS noise from stationary devices.\n    /// Default: 1.5 m/s (5.4 km/h) - reasonable threshold to filter out GPS drift.\n    static let speedThreshold: Double = 1.5 // m/s\n    /// Calculates the ghost coordinate and polylines for completed/remaining segments.\n    /// - Parameters:\n    ///   - route: The MKRoute to traverse.\n    ///   - deviceTimestamp: The last known timestamp of the remote device location.\n    ///   - knownDeviceSpeed: Optional remote device speed in meters per second.\n    ///   - userTimestamp: The last known timestamp of the local device location.\n    ///   - knownUserSpeed: Optional local device speed in meters per second.\n    ///   - now: Reference time (defaults to Date()).\n    ///   - isRouteReversed: Whether the route is reversed (device → user).         "contents": "        } else {\n            // Fallback: use expectedTravelTime proportion if available (start appears stationary)\n            let expected = route.expectedTravelTime\n            let progress = expected &gt; 0 ? max(0, min(1, fallbackElapsed / expected)) : 0\n            distanceFromStart = totalDistance * progress\n        }\n\n        // Ghost calculation follows the active route direction (start -&gt; end).\n        let splitDistance = max(0, min(totalDistance, distanceFromStart))\n        \n        guard let (splitStartToSplit, splitSplitToEnd, ghost) = route.polyline.split(at: splitDistance) else { return nil }\n        let progressValue = max(0, min(1, distanceFromStart / totalDistance))\n        \n        // Return (done, todo, ghost, progress) from route start to end.\n        return (splitStartToSplit, splitSplitToEnd, ghost, progressValue)\n    }\n\n    private static func usableSpeed(_ speed: Double?) -&gt; Double? {\n        guard let speed, speed.isFinite else { return nil }\n        return speed &gt;= speedThreshold ? speed : nil\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.",

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

        "contents": "    private func openInAppleMaps() {\n        // Open the route in the Apple Maps app using the selected transport type\n        guard let dest = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        let source: MKMapItem\n        let destination: MKMapItem\n        if isRouteReversed {\n            source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            source.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n            destination = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n        } else {\n            source = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n            destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            destination.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n        }\n        var options: [String: Any] = [:]\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeWalking\n        case 3: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeTransit\n        default: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeDriving\n        }\n        MKMapItem.openMaps(with: [source, destination], launchOptions: options)\n    }\n\n    private func transportTypeFromSetting(_ value: Int) -&gt; MKDirectionsTransportType {\n        switch value {\n        case 0: return .walking\n        case 3: return .transit\n        default: return .automobile\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func showErrorOverlay(_ debugMessage: String, _ userMessage: String) {\n        debugLog(\"Error: \\(debugMessage)\")\n        errorOverlayManager.show(message: userMessage, animationsAllowed: animationsAllowed)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Remote updates for the selected device only\n\n    private func fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: Bool, ignoreRouteCache: Bool = false) async {\n        // Fetch latest location for just the selected device from the server.",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/navigation_overlay_mode_a06f0fbb.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {

        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\n\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\n\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\n\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\n\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "    private func refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed, let route else {\n            navigationOverlayViewModel = nil\n            lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n            return\n        }\n        // Create and fully configure the view model before assigning so the view never shows\n        // the kit's default step (e.g. \"Arrive at destination\") for a frame when switching route\n        let newViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: navigationOverlayUnit())\n        let effectiveStepIndex: Int\n        if let location = locationManager.currentLocation,\n           let rawStepIndex = closestStepIndex(for: route, to: location.coordinate) {\n            // Never show \"Arrive at destination\" unless user is actually near the destination:\n            // if closest step is the last step, check distance to route end; if far, use step 0\n            let lastIndex = route.steps.count - 1\n            if rawStepIndex == lastIndex, lastIndex &gt; 0 {\n                let lastStep = route.steps[lastIndex]\n                let userPoint = MKMapPoint(location.coordinate)\n                let distanceToDestination = lastStep.polyline.closestDistance(to: userPoint) ?? .greatestFiniteMagnitude\n                if distanceToDestination &gt; 150 {\n                    effectiveStepIndex = 0\n                } else {\n                    effectiveStepIndex = rawStepIndex\n                }\n            } else {\n                effectiveStepIndex = rawStepIndex\n            }\n            let step = route.steps[effectiveStepIndex]\n            newViewModel.update(step: effectiveStepIndex)\n            if let remainingMeters = step.polyline.remainingDistance(toEndFrom: MKMapPoint(location.coordinate)) {\n                let measurement = Measurement(value: remainingMeters, unit: UnitLength.meters)\n                    .converted(to: navigationOverlayUnit())\n                newViewModel.updateRemainingDistance(to: measurement)\n            } else {\n                let fallback = Measurement(value: step.distance, unit: UnitLength.meters)\n                    ",

        "contents": "        ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing) {\n            Image(systemName: \"arrow.clockwise\")\n                .foregroundStyle(isAutoRouteUpdateLocked ? Color.green : Color.primary)\n                .symbolEffect(.rotate.clockwise.byLayer, options: .nonRepeating, isActive: isUpdating)\n                .padding(.horizontal, 6)\n                .padding(.vertical, 8)\n                .contentShape(Rectangle())\n                .onTapGesture {\n                    if animationsAllowed {\n                        withAnimation { isUpdating = true }\n                    } else {\n                        isUpdating = true\n                    }\n                    Task {\n                        await fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: true, ignoreRouteCache: true)\n                        if animationsAllowed {\n                            withAnimation { isUpdating = false }\n                        } else {\n                            isUpdating = false\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                .onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.6) {\n                    // Toggle global setting for automatic route updates while navigating\n                    settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation.toggle()\n                    isAutoRouteUpdateLocked = settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation\n                    if settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation {\n                        Haptic.notifySuccess()\n                        calculateRoute()\n                    } else {\n                        Haptic.notifyWarning()\n                    }\n                }\n                .accessibilityLabel(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload\", comment: \"Reload target device location\")))\n                .accessibilityHint(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload_longpress_hint\", comment: \"Long-press to toggle automatic route updates.\")))\n        }\n        .animation(animationsAllowed ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : nil, value: isAutoRouteUpdateLocked)\n        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)\n    }",

        "contents": "    static func ghost(for route: MKRoute, deviceTimestamp: Date?, knownDeviceSpeed: Double?, userTimestamp: Date?, knownUserSpeed: Double?, now: Date = Date(), isRouteReversed: Bool = false) -&gt; (MKPolyline, MKPolyline, CLLocationCoordinate2D, Double)? {\n        guard route.distance &gt; 0 else { return nil }\n        let totalDistance = route.distance\n        \n        // Only use speeds above the threshold to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices\n        let deviceSpeed = usableSpeed(knownDeviceSpeed)\n        let userSpeed = usableSpeed(knownUserSpeed)\n        \n        // Use the speed/timestamp of the journey start to keep progress aligned to route direction.\n        let primarySpeed = isRouteReversed ? deviceSpeed : userSpeed\n        let primaryTimestamp = isRouteReversed ? deviceTimestamp : userTimestamp\n        let secondaryTimestamp = isRouteReversed ? userTimestamp : deviceTimestamp\n        \n        let fallbackElapsed: TimeInterval\n        if let primaryTimestamp {\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(primaryTimestamp)\n        } else if let secondaryTimestamp {\n            fallbackElapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(secondaryTimestamp)\n        } else {\n            fallbackElapsed = 0\n        }\n        \n        let distanceFromStart: CLLocationDistance\n        if let speed = primarySpeed {\n            if let ts = primaryTimestamp {\n                let elapsed = max(0, now.timeIntervalSince(ts))\n                distanceFromStart = min(totalDistance, max(0, elapsed * speed))\n            } else {\n                // Without a timestamp we cannot project using speed; fall back to travel time\n                let expected = route.expectedTravelTime\n                let progress = expected &gt; 0 ? max(0, min(1, fallbackElapsed / expected)) : 0\n                distanceFromStart = totalDistance * progress\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Fallback: use expectedTravelTime proportion if available (start appears stationary)",

        "contents": "    private func updateNavigationOverlayStep() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed,\n              let route,\n              let navigationOverlayViewModel,\n              let location = locationManager.currentLocation else { return }\n        guard var stepIndex = closestStepIndex(for: route, to: location.coordinate) else { return }\n        // Never show \"Arrive at destination\" unless user is actually near the destination\n        let lastIndex = route.steps.count - 1\n        if stepIndex == lastIndex, lastIndex &gt; 0 {\n            let lastStep = route.steps[lastIndex]\n            let userPoint = MKMapPoint(location.coordinate)\n            let distanceToDestination = lastStep.polyline.closestDistance(to: userPoint) ??                   "content": "// MARK: - Route Ghost Calculator"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15,
                  "content": "/// Computes a ghost/predicted position along a route, optionally weighting by known device speed."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 19,
                  "content": "struct RouteGhostCalculator {"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 24,
                  "content": "    /// Calculates the ghost coordinate and polylines for completed/remaining segments."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 33,
                  "content": "    /// - Returns: (donePolyline, todoPolyline, ghostCoordinate, progress [0,1]) or nil if cannot compute."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 34,
                  "content": "    static func ghost(for route: MKRoute, deviceTimestamp: Date?, knownDeviceSpeed: Double?, userTimestamp: Date?, knownUserSpeed: Double?, now: Date = Date(), isRouteReversed: Bool = false) -&gt; (MKPolyline, MKPolyline, CLLocationCoordinate2D, Double)? {"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 74,
                  "content": "        // Ghost calculation follows the active route direction (start -&gt; end)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 77,
                  "content": "        guard let (splitStartToSplit, splitSplitToEnd, ghost) = route.polyline.split(at: splitDistance) else { return nil }"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 80,
                  "content": "        // Return (done, todo, ghost, progress) from route start to end."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 81,
                  "content": "        return (splitStartToSplit, splitSplitToEnd, ghost, progressValue)"
                }
              ]
            },

The change wraps the ghost rendering (the `MapCircle` and `Annotation` components) in a `if !isRouteReversed` check, so it only displays in the default navigation direction. The route progress visualization (completed/remaining segments) still shows in both directions; only the ghost marker is conditionally hidden.

No linter errors. Ready to test.

Committed the fix.

## Summary

**Problem:** The ghost marker was shown on the map even when navigation was reversed (user navigating towards device), which was incorrect.

**Solution:** Added a conditional check `if !isRouteReversed` around the ghost marker rendering (the `MapCircle` and `Annotation` components). The ghost now only appears in the default navigation direction (device navigating towards user), where it represents the other device's progress along the route.

**Changes:**
- Modified `iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift` to conditionally render the ghost marker
- Added a comment explaining when the ghost should be displayed
- The route progress visualization (completed/remaining segments) still works in both directions; only the ghost marker is conditionally hidden

**Commit:** `1ac7c43a` - "Fix ghost marker display on reversed navigation routes"

The fix is committed and ready. The ghost marker will now only appear when appropriate.
